timeline.summary: On 20 April 2026 CEAT approved a ₹3.25 Cr cash subscription to 26,626 equity shares of its wholly owned subsidiary Tyresnmore Online Private Limited via a rights issue, keeping its stake at 100%, with allotment due by 8 May 2026.
CEAT incorporated a German step-down subsidiary, CEAT GMBH, with a capital of Euro 25,000.
Commissioner CGST & Central Excise quashed 4 SCNs demanding ₹276.7 Cr differential excise duty on tyre set assembly without penalty.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹4,218.89 Cr, net profit ₹243.8 Cr.
On 28 April 2026, CEAT reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹4,218.9 Cr and net profit of ₹243.8 Cr.
On 29 April 2026, CEAT provided the audio recording link for its Q4 FY26 earnings call.

On 25 May 2026, CEAT filed an investor presentation for the RPG Annual Investor Conference setting a Vision 2031 target of #1 in 2W/4W tyres and 15% commercial radial share, with CAMSO brand migration by Sep 2028.

On 4 June 2026, CEAT disclosed a rectified GST order (DRC-08, 3 June 2026) cutting a Tamil Nadu FY2019-20 demand to ₹3.2 Cr tax and ₹3.2 Cr penalty from ₹4.7 Cr each, with no material impact expected.
Q2FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹4,762 Cr (+26.2% YoY), net profit to shareholders ₹26 Cr (-86.0% YoY).
